ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the isosceles $\triangle ABC$, where $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=50^\circ$, the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ at point $E$. By folding along $FG$ such that point $C$ coincides with point $E$, what is the measure of $\angle CFG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BE,

$\because$ $\angle BAC=50^\circ$ and AE is the bisector of $\angle BAC$,

$\therefore$ $\angle BAE = \frac{1}{2} \times 50^\circ = 25^\circ$.

Moreover, $\because$ AB=AC,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=65^\circ$.

$\because$ DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB,

$\therefore$ EA=EB,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABE=\angle BAE=25^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle EBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABE=65^\circ-25^\circ=40^\circ$.

$\because$ AE is the bisector of $\angle BAC$ and AB=AC,

$\therefore$ The line AE bisects BC perpendicularly,

$\therefore$ EB=EC,

$\therefore$ $\angle ECB=\angle EBC=40^\circ$,

$\because$ $\angle ACB$ is folded along FG,

$\therefore$ EF=CF,

$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=\angle ECF=40^\circ$;

In $\triangle ECF$, $\angle EFC=180^\circ-\angle CEF-\angle ECF=180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=100^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle CFG = \frac{1}{2} \times \angle CFE = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

Segment AE goes downward from A through interior point E to point F on the base, looking like the angle bisector/symmetry axis of the vertex angle. Point D is on AB, and the straight line D-E-G passes through E and is perpendicular to AB at D, representing the perpendicular bisector of AB; point G is on AC. There is also crease FG, from F on the base to G on AC, and after folding, C coincides with E. Reasoning: Because AB=AC and ∠BAC=50°, the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-50°)/2=65°. AE is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, so ∠BAE=25°. E is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, therefore EA=EB, and △ABE is an isosceles triangle, obtaining ∠ABE=∠BAE=25°. Thus ∠EBC=∠ABC-∠ABE=65°-25°=40°. Also because in isosceles triangle ABC, the vertex angle bisector AE is also the perpendicular bisector of BC, and E is on AE, so EB=EC. Therefore in △EBC, ∠ECB=∠EBC=40°. Since F is on BC, ray CF is in the same direction as CB, so ∠ECF=40°. Folding along FG makes C coincide with E, therefore the distances from F to C and E are equal, that is, FC=FE, and FG is the angle bisector of the two rays FC and FE before and after folding. Thus in △CEF, ∠CEF=∠ECF=40°, so ∠CFE=180°-40°-40°=100°. Therefore ∠CFG=half of ∠CFE=50°.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: read the image as an isosceles triangle ABC with A at the top, BC horizontal, AE drawn down the symmetry line to F on BC, E on AE, D on AB with DE perpendicular to AB, and a fold crease FG from F on BC to G on AC; the fold sends C to E. Because AE is also the perpendicular bisector/median of BC in the isosceles triangle, E lies on the symmetry axis, so EB=EC, giving angle ECB=40°. Since F lies on BC in the image, angle ECF=40°. The fold taking C to E means FG is the perpendicular bisector of CE and also the angle bisector of angle CFE, with FC reflected to FE. Thus triangle CEF has base angles 40° and 40°, so angle CFE=100°, and angle CFG=50°.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个等腰三角形 ABC，A 在上方，B 在左下方，C 在右下方，底边 BC 近似水平。线段 AE 从 A 向下经过内部点 E 到达底边上的点 F，看起来是顶角的角平分线/对称轴。点 D 在 AB 上，直线 D-E-G 穿过 E，并与 AB 垂直于 D，表示 AB 的垂直平分线；点 G 在 AC 上。另有折痕 FG，从底边上的 F 连到 AC 上的 G，折叠后 C 与 E 重合。

推理：因为 AB=AC 且 ∠BAC=50°，所以底角 ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-50°)/2=65°。AE 是 ∠BAC 的角平分线，所以 ∠BAE=25°。E 在 AB 的垂直平分线上，因此 EA=EB，△ABE 为等腰三角形，得到 ∠ABE=∠BAE=25°。于是 ∠EBC=∠ABC-∠ABE=65°-25°=40°。又因为在等腰三角形 ABC 中，顶角角平分线 AE 也是 BC 的垂直平分线，E 在 AE 上，所以 EB=EC。因此 △EBC 中 ∠ECB=∠EBC=40°。由于 F 在 BC 上，射线 CF 与 CB 同向，所以 ∠ECF=40°。折叠沿 FG 使 C 与 E 重合，因此 F 到 C、E 的距离相等，即 FC=FE，且 FG 是折叠前后两条射线 FC 与 FE 的角平分线。于是 △CEF 中 ∠CEF=∠ECF=40°，所以 ∠CFE=180°-40°-40°=100°。因此 ∠CFG=一半的 ∠CFE=50°。

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: read the image with AE as the vertical symmetry line of the isosceles triangle, B and C symmetric on the horizontal base, E on AE, and the fold crease FG through F on BC so that C reflects to E. Use coordinates instead of angle chasing. From the text, set A=(0,h), B=(-t,0), C=(t,0), with AE the y-axis. Since AE bisects the 50° apex angle, the side AC makes 25° with AE, so t/h=tan25°. Let E=(0,e). Because E lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, EA=EB, so (h-e)^2=t^2+e^2, hence h^2-2he=t^2 and e=(h^2-t^2)/(2h). Then the slope direction of CE has vertical-to-horizontal ratio e/t, while the fold line FG is the perpendicular bisector of CE, so its slope relative to the positive horizontal direction CF is t/e. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the isosceles $\triangle ABC$, where $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=50^\circ$, the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ at point $E$. By folding along $FG$ such that point $C$ coincides with point $E$, what is the measure of $\angle CFG$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BE,

$\because$ $\angle BAC=50^\circ$ and AE is the bisector of $\angle BAC$,

$\therefore$ $\angle BAE = \frac{1}{2} \times 50^\circ = 25^\circ$.

Moreover, $\because$ AB=AC,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=65^\circ$.

$\because$ DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB,

$\therefore$ EA=EB,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABE=\angle BAE=25^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle EBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABE=65^\circ-25^\circ=40^\circ$.

$\because$ AE is the bisector of $\angle BAC$ and AB=AC,

$\therefore$ The line AE bisects BC perpendicularly,

$\therefore$ EB=EC,

$\therefore$ $\angle ECB=\angle EBC=40^\circ$,

$\because$ $\angle ACB$ is folded along FG,

$\therefore$ EF=CF,

$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=\angle ECF=40^\circ$;

In $\triangle ECF$, $\angle EFC=180^\circ-\angle CEF-\angle ECF=180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=100^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle CFG = \frac{1}{2} \times \angle CFE = \boxed{50^\circ}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is an isosceles triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and base BC approximately horizontal. Segment AE goes downward from A through interior point E to point F on the base, looking like the angle bisector/symmetry axis of the vertex angle. Point D is on AB, and the straight line D-E-G passes through E and is perpendicular to AB at D, representing the perpendicular bisector of AB; point G is on AC. There is also crease FG, from F on the base to G on AC, and after folding, C coincides with E.

Reasoning: Because AB=AC and ∠BAC=50°, the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-50°)/2=65°. AE is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, so ∠BAE=25°. E is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, therefore EA=EB, and △ABE is an isosceles triangle, obtaining ∠ABE=∠BAE=25°. Thus ∠EBC=∠ABC-∠ABE=65°-25°=40°. Also because in isosceles triangle ABC, the vertex angle bisector AE is also the perpendicular bisector of BC, and E is on AE, so EB=EC. Therefore in △EBC, ∠ECB=∠EBC=40°. Since F is on BC, ray CF is in the same direction as CB, so ∠ECF=40°. Folding along FG makes C coincide with E, therefore the distances from F to C and E are equal, that is, FC=FE, and FG is the angle bisector of the two rays FC and FE before and after folding. Thus in △CEF, ∠CEF=∠ECF=40°, so ∠CFE=180°-40°-40°=100°. Therefore ∠CFG=half of ∠CFE=50°.
